```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
```

# Introduction
This challenge explores all matches of Italian soccer Serie A league from 1993 to current year. The dataset is contained in the website football-data.co.uk. The data is presented as a list of .csv files that have to be retrieved, parsed and polished to be usable with tidyr and dplyr.

# Scraping the data

This data scraping code has been largely generated by Posit Assistant using Gemma4-26B-A4B (Q_4) run locally with the canonical snap inference thinking=off, with some human adjustments (data parsing).

```{r}
# Define the range of seasons to scrape
# The pattern for seasons is YY/YY (e.g., 9394 for 1993/1994)
# We start from 1993/1994 up to 2025/2026 (as per the webfetch example)

# Helper to generate season strings
generate_season_strings <- function(start_year, end_year) {
  map(start_year:end_year, ~ {
    y1 <- substr(as.character(.x), 3, 4)
    y2 <- substr(as.character(.x + 1), 3, 4)
    paste0(y1, y2)
  })
}

seasons <- generate_season_strings(1993, 2026)

# Base URL pattern
base_url <- "https://football-data.co.uk/mmz4281/"

# Construct full URLs for I1.csv (Serie A)
urls <- map_chr(seasons, ~ paste0(base_url, .x, "/I1.csv"))

# Function to safely read and select columns
fetch_season_data <- function(url) {
  tryCatch({
    read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      select(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG) |>
      filter(!is.na(Date)) |>
      mutate(Date = dmy(Date))
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("Failed to fetch:", url))
    return(NULL)
  })
}

# Scrape all seasons and bind together
all_matches <- urls |>
  map(fetch_season_data) |>
  list_rbind()

# Inspect the result
all_matches |> head()
```

# Extracting more per-team information
With the following part we're going to extract more information from the data, adding a column with the computed outcome of the match (H = home teams wins, A = away team wins, P = draw).

```{r}
all_matches <- all_matches |> 
  mutate(Outcome = case_when(
    FTHG > FTAG ~ "H",
    FTHG < FTAG ~ "A",
    TRUE        ~ "P"
  ))
all_matches
```

# Calculate W/L/P 

We can calculate win / loss / draw by computing tha values from the data, knowing that the logical check on the goals is inverted if the team plays away.

```{r}
home_stats <- all_matches |>
  mutate(Outcome = case_when(
    FTHG > FTAG ~ "W",
    FTHG < FTAG ~ "L",
    TRUE        ~ "P"
  )) |>
  group_by(Team = HomeTeam, Outcome) |>
  summarise(matches = n(), .groups = "drop")

away_stats <- all_matches |>
  mutate(Outcome = case_when(
    FTHG > FTAG ~ "L",
    FTHG < FTAG ~ "W",
    TRUE        ~ "P"
  )) |>
  group_by(Team = AwayTeam, Outcome) |>
  summarise(matches = n(), .groups = "drop")
home_stats
away_stats
```

# Calculate aggregate W/L/P
Now we need to bind the rows together and group by team and outcome to obtain the number of win / loss / draw for every team. Then we can use pivot_wider to create new columns W/L/P from the Outcome column.

```{r}
final_stats <- bind_rows(home_stats, away_stats) |>
  group_by(Team, Outcome) |>
  summarise(total_matches = sum(matches), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Outcome, values_from = total_matches, values_fill = 0)
final_stats
```
# Calculate last metrics
Now we can calculate the last metrics: Points and Points per match.

```{r}
final_stats <- final_stats |>
  mutate(
    Total = W+L+P,
  )
final_stats

final_stats <- final_stats |>
  mutate(
    Points = (W * 3) + (P * 1),
    PPM = Points / Total
  )
final_stats
```
# Interesting questions
Some questions with an interesting potential:
 1) What has been the most predictable team in terms of outcome from the Bet365 quotations? And the most unpredictable?
 2) Who was the most aggressive (fouls) team? And the one that played in a more fail-play way?
 3) What team has seen the most crowd attendance growth over the years? And what team have see the most crowd decline?
